aggregate.finding: Composing Raoult (1887), Dalton (1802) and the OSHA additive mixture rule reduces EXACTLY to a mole-fraction-weighted sum of the module's existing pure-component VHRs, which supplies the blend-level index the single-substance receipts lacked. Two operational consequences follow. (i) Thinner specs are written in mass fractions; using them directly as weights mis-states the blend hazard index because the panel's molar masses span 3.3x. (ii) The dominant contributor is set by mole fraction times VHR, not by VHR alone, so a trace fast solvent has a closed-form dominance-crossover mass fraction above which it governs the ventilation requirement -- for methanol carried over into an aromatic thinner that crossover sits at a few weight percent.

h0_mass_surrogate.hypothesis: H0_MASS_SURROGATE: mass-fraction weighting of pure-component VHRs is an adequate surrogate for the mole-fraction-correct Raoult blend index.
h0_mass_surrogate.interpretation: Refuted. Reading a thinner spec's mass fractions as if they were mole fractions mis-states, with a blend-dependent SIGN, the saturated-headspace mixture hazard index by up to 39.34% across the 15-40 C envelope. Mechanism: the panel's molar masses span 32.04-106.17 g/mol (3.31x), so on conversion to mole fractions the LIGHTER constituents are up-weighted and the heavier ones down-weighted. The sign of the resulting error therefore depends on whether a blend's light constituent is more hazardous than its heavy one: in methanol- and MEK-bearing blends the light constituent carries the higher VHR and mass weighting UNDER-states the index (worst case -37.63%), whereas in the xylene/n-butanol thinner the lighter alcohol is the LESS hazardous constituent and mass weighting OVER-states it (1.74%). A single directional correction factor is therefore not available; the mole-fraction conversion has to be done.

h0_pure_worst_actor.hypothesis: H0_PURE_WORST_ACTOR: the constituent with the highest pure-component VHR is the dominant contributor to the blend's inhalation hazard.
h0_pure_worst_actor.interpretation: Refuted on at least one realistic blend: the pure-component worst actor is NOT always the dominant blend contributor, because contribution scales with mole fraction. A trace high-volatility solvent can be the single worst substance on the shelf and still be a minor contributor below its dominance-crossover mass fraction -- and can take over above it. Single-substance VHR prescreening therefore mis-assigns the ventilation-priority target for blends near the crossover.

kpis.authority_ceiling_note: EVIDENCE_ONLY quantitative BLEND-level inhalation-hazard PRESCREEN. Apportions intrinsic saturated-headspace hazard among a thinner blend's constituents to target engineering ventilation and to flag trace constituents that govern. Assumes ideal-solution Raoult behaviour (declared, with gamma_crit sensitivity reported) and saturated headspace, which is a bounding rather than a realised exposure. Does NOT establish OSHA compliance, exposure assessment, control banding, respirator selection, procurement approval, or regulatory closure.
kpis.blend_composition_provenance: Blend mass fractions are illustrative rights-clean scenarios constructed to span the marine 2K epoxy-amine thinner design space (aromatic-rich, ketone-boosted fast, alcohol-rich anti-blush, wash-solvent carryover). They are NOT vendor formulations and encode no supplier-proprietary composition. The physical conclusions (identity exactness, mass-vs-mole surrogate error, closed-form dominance crossover) are properties of the solvents' molar masses, vapour pressures and PELs, not of the illustrative fractions.

crossover_empirical_validation.rationale: Pairwise dominance between two constituents is invariant to the rest of the blend because the mole-fraction normalisation cancels in the contribution ratio, so the closed form is exact for this ternary series, not an approximation.

kpis.formula: MHI_sat(blend,T) = sum_i x_i*gamma_i*VHR_i(T); x_i from mass fractions via x_i=(w_i/M_i)/sum_j(w_j/M_j); VHR_i(T)=(P_i^0(T)/760)*1e6/PEL_i; gamma_i=1 (ideal, declared)
kpis.ideality_declaration: Raoult's law is applied with gamma_i = 1. For alcohol + aromatic blends positive deviation (gamma_alcohol > 1) is expected, so the ideal MHI is a LOWER bound for those blends. No activity coefficients are invented; the dominance calls are instead stress-tested by reporting gamma_crit.

kpis.pel_denominator_source: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1000 Table Z-1 (8-hour TWA permissible exposure limits) with the additive mixture rule at 1910.1000(d)(2)(i); U.S. federal regulation, public domain

probe_corrupted_formula.explanation: A corrupted declared formula (C9H12 for m-xylene, true C8H10) must be caught by the RDKit structure-vs-formula cross-check before its molar mass can enter a mole-fraction conversion.

probe_non_admitted_solvent.explanation: MIBK (4-methyl-2-pentanone) has no rights-clean Antoine set admitted by the +/-15% PubChem concordance gate, so its partial pressure cannot be propagated. The whole blend is abstained rather than scored on a 60% subset.

probe_unnormalised_blend.explanation: Mass fractions sum to 0.90, not 1.0. A silent renormalisation would invent 10 wt% of unspecified material; the guard rejects the blend instead.

receipt_meta.data_extraction_method: Antoine coefficients and OSHA Table Z-1 PELs carried over unchanged from the module's already-signed vhr-temperature-envelope-v1 receipt; molar masses re-derived from SMILES via RDKit and cross-checked against declared molecular formulae. No LLM-authored constants, no fitted parameters, no RNG.

kpis.relationship_to_prior_receipts: First BLEND-level receipt in the module. benchmarks/vapor-hazard-ratio-v1 (Popendorf 2006) scores single substances at 25 C; benchmarks/vhr-temperature-envelope-v1 propagates those single substances over 15-40 C with the Antoine sets validated in benchmarks/antoine-vp-crosscheck-v1. This benchmark composes Raoult (1887) + Dalton (1802) + the OSHA additive mixture rule on top of exactly those pinned VHR(T) values and shows the chain reduces exactly to sum_i x_i*VHR_i -- so the prior receipts are recovered as the x_i=1 special case. It then adjudicates two hypotheses the single-substance receipts could not pose: whether mass-fraction weighting is an adequate surrogate for mole-fraction weighting, and whether the pure-component worst actor is the dominant blend contributor.
theory_references: Raoult, F.-M. (1887) 'Loi generale des tensions de vapeur des dissolvants', Comptes Rendus de l'Academie des Sciences 104: 1430-1433 (partial pressure proportional to mole fraction).
Dalton, J. (1802) 'Experimental Essays on the Constitution of Mixed Gases', Memoirs of the Literary and Philosophical Society of Manchester 5: 535-602 (additivity of partial pressures).
OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1000(d)(2)(i) (additive mixture exposure rule E_m = sum C_i/L_i) and Table Z-1 (8-hr TWA permissible exposure limits); U.S. federal regulation, public domain.

Popendorf, W. (2006) Industrial Hygiene Control of Airborne Chemical Hazards, CRC Press, ISBN 978-0-8247-2719-2, Ch. 3 (Vapor Hazard Ratio; the single-substance gamma=1, x=1 special case of the index composed here).
Antoine, C. (1888) 'Tensions des vapeurs; nouvelle relation entre les tensions et les temperatures', Comptes Rendus de l'Academie des Sciences 107: 681-684, 778-780, 836-837.
Dean, J.A. (ed.) (1999) Lange's Handbook of Chemistry, 15th ed., McGraw-Hill, Table 5.28 (Antoine vapour-pressure constants). ISBN 978-0-07-016384-3.
IUPAC (2021) 'Standard Atomic Weights of the Elements 2021', Pure and Applied Chemistry 93(12): 1571-1582 (atomic weights underlying the RDKit-derived molar masses).
